$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.6,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.6/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 64dd8b8b44102e3fe336f6d2328776c389cee2914787759fbe3575b114d680bd and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.6/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
64dd8b8b44102e3fe336f6d2328776c389cee2914787759fbe3575b114d680bd is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
